The bottom line

Book Sun Dek Beach House: a 3-minute walk to a quiet beach, about 18 minutes to Grandma's place and excellent reviews, for $2,120 all-in, but only 2 studios were left. Sun Dek Beach House

Ocean Ridge & east Boynton · 3-min walk · Boutique hotel
75fit
$530/night all-in
$2,120 for 4 nights, all-in · $471/night before tax

✓ Few rooms left for Feb 18–22 — checked Oct 16, 7:13pm via the property’s own site: Studio, $2,120 all-in ($530/night), refundable, only 2 left

A 3-minute walk through Ocean Ridge Hammock Park to a quiet beach, about 18 minutes by car to Grandma's place, and top reviews (Booking.com 9.6, Google 4.8). The Studio has a king bed and a full kitchen, with free beach chairs and umbrellas and a heated saltwater pool, for $2,120 all-in ($530 a night), refundable. Only 2 studios were left when we checked, and there's nowhere to eat within an easy walk, so plan to drive or cook for dinner.

  • Beach7/10 · About a 3-minute walk across quiet two-lane A1A and through the Ocean Ridge Hammock Park path to an uncrowded, recently renourished beach. It is unguarded, which keeps it from a higher score.
  • Grandma8/10 · Routed at 17-18 minutes (8.0 mi) by car, between the 15-minute and 22-minute anchors. The Ocean Ave drawbridge (openings on the hour and half-hour) can add a few minutes.

Berkshire on the Ocean (Airbnb unit)

Delray south beach · Beachfront · Whole-home rental · Airbnb

✓ Bookable for Feb 18–22 — checked Oct 16, 10:17pm via Airbnb: Berkshire on the Ocean, $1,688 all-in ($422/night)

A one-bedroom unit at a small resort at the south end of Delray's beach: a gate opens onto its own sand with free cabanas and loungers, and the public Atlantic Dunes Park access is 2-3 minutes north. Rated 4.94 from 34 reviews, with a Superhost manager, on-site staff and a heated pool. $1,688 all-in with estimated taxes ($422 a night); Airbnb showed $1,500 before taxes. The drive to Grandma's place is about 28 minutes, near your limit, and the second bed is a pull-out sofa, so ask the host which bed size your unit has.

  • Beach9/10 · Beachfront: a private dune gate opens onto the resort's own uncrowded sand with cabanas, and the public Atlantic Dunes Park access is 2-3 minutes north.
  • Grandma5/10 · About 25 min free-flow and roughly 28 min in daytime traffic, near the 30-minute outer limit, with a drawbridge on the way.

The lowest all-in price of any place that passed your must-haves: a remodeled king room for $726 all-in ($182 a night), refundable, and the last one of that type when we checked. Downtown Lantana restaurants are 2-5 minutes away and Grandma's place is about 24 minutes by car. A 2-3 minute walk over the A1A crosswalk to Delray's lifeguarded public beach, and 11-15 minutes on foot to the Atlantic Ave restaurants, with four bars and restaurants on site and a big ocean-view pool. A King Standard View room is $3,472 all-in ($868 a night) including the resort fee, refundable until Feb 11. Grandma's place is about 28 minutes by car, near your limit; the hotel has no beach chairs (rent them on the beach) and valet parking is extra.

  • Beach7/10 · A 2-3 minute walk over the A1A crosswalk at Atlantic Ave to Delray's wide, lifeguarded Blue Flag public beach, renourished in early 2026; not on the sand, and the Atlantic Ave end is the busiest stretch.
  • Grandma5/10 · Google Maps puts a typical Thursday-morning February drive at 28 min (range 22-40) over 11.2 mi, between the 22- and 30-minute anchors; the Atlantic Ave drawbridge can add a few minutes.

✓ Bookable for Feb 18–22 — checked Oct 16, 5:44pm via the property’s own site: Ocean View King, $7,000 all-in ($1,750/night), refundable

A full-service resort on its own sand, with beach chairs and umbrellas included, two heated oceanfront pools (one adults-only), a large spa and no resort fee. Staff score 9.4 on Booking.com, and Grandma's place is about 23 minutes by car. An Ocean View King is $7,000 all-in ($1,750 a night), free to cancel until Feb 4. Balcony work on the room towers will likely be under way, so ask for a room away from it.

  • Beach8/10 · On its own sand with calm, swimmable water and the public Lantana beach next door; docked from a 10 because this Manalapan stretch is state-listed as critically eroded and the sand narrows sharply at high tide.
  • Grandma6/10 · About 22-23 minutes and 11-12 miles by car in free-flow routing, so typical daytime traffic and a possible Lantana drawbridge opening put it a bit past the 22-minute anchor, inside the 30-minute limit.

17-unit renovated 1960s beach motel across A1A from a quiet Ocean Ridge beach, with a heated saltwater pool, full kitchens and free beach chairs.

Best for: A couple who wants a quiet, beach-across-the-street base with a kitchen, a short drive from Grandma, and doesn't mind driving or cooking for dinner.

How it scores

75Fit score 75/100

Beach access7/10
About a 3-minute walk across quiet two-lane A1A and through the Ocean Ridge Hammock Park path to an uncrowded, recently renourished beach. It is unguarded, which keeps it from a higher score.
Drive to Grandma8/10
Routed at 17-18 minutes (8.0 mi) by car, between the 15-minute and 22-minute anchors. The Ocean Ave drawbridge (openings on the hour and half-hour) can add a few minutes.
Cleanliness9/10
Booking.com cleanliness 9.6 and Tripadvisor cleanliness 4.9, with daily housekeeping praised in 2026 reviews and no recurring cleanliness complaints found.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Beach chairs, umbrellas and towels are lent free and guests carry them to a quiet beach, so there is no scramble for space; March guests mention them, with no shortage reports.
Pool7/10
One heated (and chilled) saltwater pool, 4-8 ft deep, in a landscaped courtyard shared by only 17 units; good for a swim and rarely busy, but not large.
Condition & newness7/10
1962 buildings renovated in 2014 and kept in very good shape; 2025-26 guests call it fresh and well kept, with only small bathrooms, few mirrors and older TVs (being replaced) mentioned.
Service9/10
Booking.com staff 9.8 and Tripadvisor service 4.9; office staff (Marsha is named repeatedly) and the general manager, who answers reviews, are praised in many reviews.
Quiet9/10
A small courtyard property in residential Ocean Ridge on a light-traffic stretch of A1A; 2026 reviews call the area very quiet and no construction is expected next door.
Walkable dining2/10
Nothing to eat in residential Ocean Ridge: the nearest sit-down restaurants are at Boynton Harbor Marina, a 22-25 minute walk over the Ocean Ave drawbridge, so most meals mean a drive or the in-room kitchen.
Host reliability8/10
A long-running independent hotel whose units match their photos and descriptions in reviews, with no reports of cancelled bookings; its cancellation terms are strict, though.

Beach notes
Ocean Ridge Hammock Park: county beach, unguarded, outdoor shower, no restroom, open sunrise to sunset. Quiet, mostly residential stretch; the Army Corps renourished the beach here from March 2026. Man o' war can wash up November-April. Boynton Beach Oceanfront Park is a 7-minute walk south.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • About 3 minutes on foot to a quiet, recently renourished beach
  • About 18 minutes by car to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach
  • Exceptional reviews: Booking.com 9.6, Google 4.8, Tripadvisor 4.9
  • Free beach chairs, umbrellas and towels from the office
  • Heated saltwater pool, shared BBQs and a gazebo
  • Full kitchen and daily housekeeping; free parking
  • Very quiet residential setting; only 17 units
Cons
  • Nowhere to eat within an easy walk: the nearest restaurants are 22+ minutes away over a drawbridge
  • Beach in front is unguarded, with no restroom
  • 1962 motel buildings: bathrooms are small and TVs older
  • Strict cancellation terms: a quarter of the booking is charged inside the 3-30 day window
  • Only 2 studios were left for these dates when checked on Oct 16

Insider tips

  • The Studio has one king bed and sleeps exactly 2; the 1-bedroom suites add a separate bedroom and a sofa bed.
  • Ask for an Intracoastal-side room for sunset views (a Tripadvisor guest's tip; the Sunset View 1-bedroom faces west).
  • Arriving after 8 pm? Call the office (561-732-2544) ahead for access instructions.
  • Borrow beach chairs, umbrellas and towels at the office; pool floats and beach toys are in the laundry room.
  • Hammock Park beach is unguarded with only an outdoor shower; Boynton Beach Oceanfront Park is 7 minutes south.
  • Plan on a car or Uber for dinner: Boynton Harbor Marina's restaurants are the nearest, 22-25 minutes on foot.
  • The cancellation window (3-30 days) depends on arrival date; confirm the exact deadline in the booking confirmation.
  • The house policy says the person checking in must be 25 or older.

We couldn’t verify

  • Year built (1962) and renovation year (2014) are known only from commercial-listing search snippets (LoopNet, floridaparcels; both blocked) (via search snippet).
  • Pool length and hours are not published.
  • Elevator: none mentioned for the two-storey buildings; unconfirmed.
  • Google review dates are relative ('5 months ago') and converted to approximate months; Booking.com review samples are undated.
  • Tripadvisor count (408) is as shown on Google Travel in Oct 2026; the review text read is from an Aug 2025 Wayback snapshot (live Tripadvisor blocked).
  • No February review from the last 12 months was read; the nearest same-season evidence is March 2025 and March 2026 stays.
  • Beach chair supply per unit and any reservation rules are not stated.
  • Lifeguard status at Boynton Beach Oceanfront Park not checked; Hammock Park is unguarded per the county.

Scripted check of Berkshire on the Ocean (verify_listing.py). The map location is approximate.

One-bedroom unit at a 23-unit, two-story beachfront resort in south Delray, with free beach cabanas and a heated pool.

Best for: Two adults who want to walk out a gate onto quiet sand with a free cabana every morning and don't mind an older, simple unit or driving to dinner.

How it scores

73Fit score 73/100

Beach access9/10
Beachfront: a private dune gate opens onto the resort's own uncrowded sand with cabanas, and the public Atlantic Dunes Park access is 2-3 minutes north.
Drive to Grandma5/10
About 25 min free-flow and roughly 28 min in daytime traffic, near the 30-minute outer limit, with a drawbridge on the way.
Cleanliness9/10
Airbnb cleanliness 4.9 and Tripadvisor 4.8, with recent guests calling the unit spotless; one 2024 Tripadvisor guest scored cleanliness low.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Cabanas and loungers are set up on the sand at no charge and the desk lends chairs and umbrellas; cabanas are first come, first served in a busy month.

An older two-story resort kept clean, with updates under way since 2024, but recent guests still call units dated and one hit AC and water outages in Aug 2026.

Nothing within 10 minutes, but about a dozen places and three supermarkets sit 11-16 minutes away over the Linton Blvd bridge; Atlantic Ave needs an Uber.

Superhost management company with 11 years and 973 reviews, a 100% response rate and front-desk check-in; no cancellations reported, though photos cover the resort rather than one unit.

Beach notes
Resort's own sand behind the dune with a row of blue cabanas; guests describe it as private and uncrowded. Delray's south beach (to south of Atlantic Dunes Park) was set for renourishment from Jan 2026. February is man o' war season (purple flag); a July 2025 guest found heavy seaweed. No lifeguard confirmed in front of the resort.

Recent trend
Steady five-star run through 2025-26 (Airbnb 4.94, 94% five-star), with one Aug 2026 four-star on age and AC/water outages. Same-season evidence is limited but positive: Jan and Feb 2025-26 guests rated it 5.

Recent reviews, paraphrased (not exact quotes):

  • “Amazing place with great views and easy access to the beach and pool. There was a problem with the first room at check-in, and staff moved them to another within 15 minutes.”5/5, Airbnb, 2026-09
  • “Great location and kind staff, but the room is very old: several AC and water interruptions during the stay, dated decor and a cramped bathroom. No frills; fine if you know what to expect.”4/5, Airbnb, 2026-08
  • “A couple's February stay exceeded expectations: steps from the beach, walking out to their own cabana, a large, spotless and comfortable apartment on beautifully kept grounds. Would return.”5/5, Airbnb, 2026-02

Pros
  • On the sand: a private dune gate opens onto the resort's own beach with free cabanas and loungers

Insider tips

  • Ask for a second-floor unit for ocean views, or the first floor to skip stairs (Tripadvisor room tips).
  • Ask the desk for a foam topper if one of you sleeps on the pull-out sofa, and ask which bed size your assigned unit has.
  • Cabanas are first come, first served; the desk lends beach chairs and an umbrella.
  • Landex also lists other one-bedroom units here on Airbnb (listings 1071902896618325496 and 1034840964054756004), and the resort takes direct bookings with a 2-night minimum and 4 pm check-in; compare them if this one sells out.
  • The Linton Blvd drawbridge opens on the hour and half-hour, so time drives to Grandma's place around it.
  • Copy-pasting the address into navigation can mislead; navigate to 1775 S Ocean Blvd, south of Atlantic Dunes Park, not to Airbnb's map pin.

We couldn’t verify

  • Main bed size for this listing is not stated: the resort's rate page lists a King Bed unit type, an Aug 2024 Tripadvisor guest had a king, and sibling listing 1034840964054756004 says queen; confirm with the host.
  • Year built unknown: Zillow/Redfin results (via search snippet) say 1983, while another search summary said the 1960s.
  • Housekeeping frequency, pool hours and dimensions, and quiet hours are not published.
  • Airbnb minimum stay not shown; the 4-night stay was bookable, and the resort's own minimum is 2 nights.
  • Drive time is a free-flow router estimate plus an allowance; Google Maps typical traffic was not measured, and the OSRM car and foot routers were unreachable.
  • Overpass was down, so restaurant counts come from Nominatim POIs and Tripadvisor's nearby list.
  • The resort assigns units, so condition varies; listing photos are resort-wide images also in its 2024 web gallery.
  • Elevator not confirmed; the buildings are two stories and a guest suggested asking for the first floor if stairs are a problem.
  • No construction check beyond the 2026 beach renourishment noted in context.
  • Tripadvisor figures come from a Dec 2025 Wayback snapshot; the live page was not fetched.

Garden motel from the 1950s on US-1 in downtown Lantana with remodeled rooms, a 20-minute walk over the bridge to Lantana's beach.

Best for: A low-key, characterful base for visiting Grandma, if you're fine walking 20 minutes to the beach and hearing the odd train.

How it scores

43Fit score 43/100

Beach access2/10
Not on the beach: the nearest public entrance, Lantana Municipal Beach, is a 19-20 minute walk over the Intracoastal drawbridge. That is inside the trip's 20-minute limit but at its very edge, to a lifeguarded beach with rocks and a shifting reef.
Drive to Grandma6/10
About 24 minutes and 11 miles by car to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach via US-1 and Boynton Beach Blvd, inside the 30-minute limit but past the 22-minute mark.
Cleanliness5/10
Averages are good (Booking.com cleanliness 8.6, Tripadvisor 4.6) and many guests call rooms immaculate, but insects keep appearing in low reviews: ants in two early-2026 Google reviews and cockroaches in two 2024 Booking.com reviews.
Beach chairs & umbrellas1/10
The motel lists no beach chairs, umbrellas or towels, so you'd bring or rent your own for the walk to Lantana's beach.
Pool1/10
There is no pool; a guest wished there were one, and Booking.com lists none.
Condition & newness6/10
A 1950s motel whose rooms have been remodeled since about 2021 and look modern in photos, but the remodel is room by room, so some rooms are still dated, and Wi-Fi and shower pressure draw 2026 complaints.
Service6/10
Many guests praise the owner and a staff member named Michelle, and Booking.com rates staff 8.9, but recent low reviews cite a rude check-in, nobody at the desk on arrival, and owner replies that argue with complaints.
Quiet4/10

Recent trend
Polarized. The Booking.com (8.1) and Tripadvisor (4.3) averages hold, and many 2026 guests praise the gardens and remodeled rooms, but Google shows a cluster of 1-2 star reviews from Jan-Jul 2026 (ants, mismatched rooms, trains). Same-season evidence covers Feb 2025 and Jan-Mar 2026 stays.

Recent reviews, paraphrased (not exact quotes):

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • Inside the 20-minute walk limit to a lifeguarded public beach
  • About 24 minutes by car to Grandma's place
  • Lush gardens with parrots and coffee and snacks in the garden
  • Remodeled king rooms with fridge, microwave and Roku TV; daily housekeeping
  • Restaurants 2-5 minutes away, incl. the waterfront Old Key Lime House
  • Free on-site parking
Cons
  • The beach walk is 19-20 min over a drawbridge, right at your limit
  • No pool and no beach chairs
  • On US-1 with an active railway across the road; train noise in reviews
  • Polarized recent reviews: insects, rooms unlike photos, rude or absent staff
  • Weak Wi-Fi (Booking.com 5.0)
  • King rate is prepaid with phone-only cancellation and conflicting terms

Insider tips

  • The direct engine showed the cheapest King Room as the last of its type; Courtyard King and other king rooms were still listed.
  • Cancellation is by phone only and the rate policy differs from the terms page, so get the terms in writing.
  • Ask for a remodeled king set back from US-1 and the rail side, and ask for photos of the actual room before arrival.
  • Arriving late? Call ahead (561-585-0600); guests report calling a number to be checked in.
  • Bring or rent beach chairs; the motel has none. Lantana beach lifeguards work 9 am-5 pm.
  • The extended-stay page mentions a pool, but that copy belongs to sister Sunny Palms Inn; there is no pool here.
  • Check whether Lantana's beach boardwalk and pavilion rebuild has started before you go.

We couldn’t verify

  • Opening year conflicts on the official site: built in 1952 (home page) vs founded in 1962 (activities page); 1952 used.
  • Last renovation year of the King Room not published; photo files are dated 2021-2022 and remodels continued into 2026.
  • Number of rooms not published.
  • Whether the E Ocean Ave rail crossing is in a train-horn quiet zone was not verified.
  • Tripadvisor rating and sub-ratings come from a Dec 2025 Wayback snapshot; Google showed 224 Tripadvisor reviews in Oct 2026.
  • Google review dates are relative ('7 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • Drive time is Google Maps leave-now on a Friday evening in October plus free-flow Valhalla routing, not a February daytime typical.
  • Front desk hours not published.
  • Expedia and Hotels.com ratings not checked.

How it scores

65Fit score 65/100

Beach access7/10
A 2-3 minute walk over the A1A crosswalk at Atlantic Ave to Delray's wide, lifeguarded Blue Flag public beach, renourished in early 2026; not on the sand, and the Atlantic Ave end is the busiest stretch.
Drive to Grandma5/10
Google Maps puts a typical Thursday-morning February drive at 28 min (range 22-40) over 11.2 mi, between the 22- and 30-minute anchors; the Atlantic Ave drawbridge can add a few minutes.
Cleanliness8/10

Beach chairs & umbrellas2/10
The hotel provides no beach chairs or umbrellas; guests rent daily from the third-party concession on the public beach across the street, which sets them up.

A large ocean-view main pool with a whirlpool and a second villas pool, praised as huge and spotless, but in February loungers are taken by about 8:30 am.
Condition & newness6/10

Service8/10

Quiet6/10
Tripadvisor sleep quality is 4.6, but it is a busy resort with bars on the Atlantic Ave/A1A corner; the 2026 renourishment and A1A road work that caused noise complaints ended in spring 2026.
Walkable dining8/10
Four on-site restaurants and bars, Boston's on the Beach and Pizza Rustica 3-4 minutes away, and the main Atlantic Ave strip 11-15 minutes over the bridge; no grocery within 10 minutes.
Host reliability8/10
An established 276-room resort selling direct on its own engine with a refundable rate for the dates and no reviewer-reported cancellations; the SynXis link on its own site pointed to a sister hotel when checked.

Recent trend
Steady at 4.4 on Google and 4.6 on Tripadvisor. Same-season (Feb-Mar 2026) reviews were dragged down by the round-the-clock beach renourishment, which ended in spring 2026; reviews from Dec 2025 on repeatedly flag the 1980s building's elevators and room infrastructure, while staff and the pool keep winning praise.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • 2-3 minute walk across A1A to Delray's lifeguarded Blue Flag public beach, rebuilt wider in early 2026
  • Walkable: four on-site bars and restaurants, Boston's and Pizza Rustica 3-4 minutes away, the Atlantic Ave strip 11-15 minutes
  • Large ocean-view main pool plus a second villas pool and a whirlpool
  • Strong, personal service: Tripadvisor service 4.7 and a Les Clefs d'Or concierge team
  • Both king and two-queen rooms, so the bed requirement is easy to meet
Cons
  • No beach chairs or umbrellas from the hotel: rent from the beach concession each day
  • 1983 building: recent guests cite slow or broken elevators, few outlets and small standard bathrooms
  • Pool loungers are gone by about 8:30 am in season
  • About 28 minutes to Grandma's place in typical traffic (22-40), near the trip's limit
  • Valet-only parking and a nightly resort fee are extra
  • Busy corner: Atlantic Ave-facing rooms can be noisy, and the Delray Beach Open (Feb 12-21) fills downtown

Nearby

Insider tips

  • Book on Opal's own engine (reservations.opalcollection.com/opal-grand); when checked, the SynXis link on the hotel's page opened a sister hotel in Nashville.
  • Ask for a higher floor away from Atlantic Ave for quieter nights (a Feb 2026 guest's tip).
  • Claim pool loungers early or reserve a cabana or daybed through the front desk; pool chairs are first come, first served.
  • Saturday Feb 20 falls in your stay: morning yoga runs 9:30-10:30 am on the pool deck; sign up by 7 pm Friday.
  • The Atlantic Ave drawbridge opens at quarter past and quarter to the hour; allow a few extra minutes on the drive to Grandma's.
  • Guests must be 21+ to check in; check-in is 4 pm, check-out 11 am.

We couldn’t verify

  • Main pool length and pool hours are not published; heated pools and 8 am-8 pm hours appear only in a search snippet (aggregator sites), so heated and hours are left null.
  • Expedia rating of 9.2/10 is known only via search snippet with no exact count, so it is not listed in ratings; Booking.com does not list the hotel.
  • Front desk hours are not published.
  • Completion of the 2026 Delray renourishment (scheduled before May 2026) is not confirmed by a primary source; no new beach work was found for February 2027.
  • The construction a Feb 2026 guest saw on the Atlantic Ave side was not identified; FDOT's A1A project ending north of Atlantic Ave had a completion date of April 7, 2026.
  • Restaurant count within 10 minutes is an estimate (4 on site plus routed nearby places); the OSM Overpass service was unavailable for a full count.
  • Google review dates are relative ('3 months ago') and converted to approximate months; Tripadvisor sub-scores come from a May 2026 Wayback snapshot.
  • Main pool shape is judged from official photos.

309-room former Ritz-Carlton on its own Manalapan beach next to Lantana Public Beach, with two heated oceanfront pools, a big spa and Nobu.

Best for: A couple who want a full-service beachfront resort with included beach chairs, a quiet heated adults pool and Grandma about 23 minutes away, and who don't need a walkable town.

How it scores

75Fit score 75/100

Beach access8/10
On its own sand with calm, swimmable water and the public Lantana beach next door; docked from a 10 because this Manalapan stretch is state-listed as critically eroded and the sand narrows sharply at high tide.
Drive to Grandma6/10
About 22-23 minutes and 11-12 miles by car in free-flow routing, so typical daytime traffic and a possible Lantana drawbridge opening put it a bit past the 22-minute anchor, inside the 30-minute limit.
Cleanliness8/10
Booking.com cleanliness 8.9 with daily housekeeping, and recent reviewers call rooms and grounds immaculate; no recurring dirt complaints found, but the score sits below the staff and comfort marks.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Beach chairs and umbrellas are included with no resort fee and beach staff draw praise; the resort swapped its old cabanas for cantilever umbrellas. Docked because supply is 'based on availability' and no February report on chair availability was found.
Pool8/10
Two heated oceanfront pools, a family resort pool with bar and hot tub plus a quieter adults-only pool, both on decks redone in 2025-26; dimensions and hours are unpublished and the adult pool is said to be shady.
Condition & newness7/10
A 1991 building kept up with a 2022 interior renovation and 2025-26 public-area work, but a mid-2026 review says the rooms badly need updating, and balcony work starts around the trip.
Service9/10
Booking.com staff score 9.4 and many 2026 reviews name staff (reservations, spa, salon, tennis); the few complaints are a poor birthday dinner at Breeze and one guest whose complaints to management went unresolved.
Quiet6/10
A spread-out resort with a quiet adults-only pool and no party scene, but it is family-oriented with a kids club and lobby/Stir live music, and the approved balcony renovation on the room towers is likely under way in February.
Walkable dining7/10
Five on-site venues plus Plaza del Mar across A1A (Publix and four eateries) within about 5 minutes; beyond that the next restaurant is a 15-minute walk over the Lantana bridge, and reviewers note little else nearby.
Host reliability8/10
An established 309-room resort booked through its own SynXis engine and the major OTAs, with a 24-hour desk and no reviewer-reported cancellations; one 2024 guest complained of hidden extra charges and valet parking is extra.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • On its own beach, with Lantana Public Beach next door
  • Beach chairs and umbrellas included; no resort fee
  • Two heated oceanfront pools, one adults-only
  • Staff score 9.4 on Booking.com; staff named in many reviews
  • Publix and four eateries across A1A, about 5 minutes on foot
  • About 23 minutes by car to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach
  • Nobu, Angle and a 42,000 sq ft spa on site
Cons
  • Balcony renovation on the room towers likely under way in February (phased, no end date)
  • Rooms dated in places per a mid-2026 review; small showers
  • Sand narrows sharply at high tide on this critically eroded stretch
  • Valet-only parking at extra cost
  • Family resort with kids club and live music, not adults-only
  • Little to walk to beyond Plaza del Mar

Nearby

  • Resort beach · 2 min (Through the pool deck)
  • Lantana Public Beach (East Ocean Ave entrance) · 5 min (Adjoins the resort to the north; Dune Deck Cafe)
  • Publix (Plaza del Mar) · 4 min (Across A1A at Ocean Ave)
  • Plaza del Mar restaurants (Art Basil, John G's, Thaikyo, Ice Cream Club) · 5 min (John G's open for breakfast and lunch)
  • Dune Deck Cafe · 5 min (At Lantana Public Beach)
  • Old Key Lime House · 15 min (Over the Lantana bridge on the Intracoastal)

Insider tips

  • Ask at booking which tower is in the balcony-railing phase in February and request a room away from it.
  • Book the Ocean View King: the Double rooms have two full beds, which reviewers call small.
  • Check-in 4 pm, check-out noon; late check-out on request.
  • Head to the adults-only pool for quiet; it gets shade early, so the main pool or beach is sunnier.
  • Private daybeds (10am-5pm) need a reservation through concierge.
  • Lantana's Ocean Ave drawbridge opens on the hour and half-hour; allow a few extra minutes driving to Grandma's.
  • A reviewer says Amex Platinum bookings come with extra perks; check if you have it.

We couldn’t verify

  • Year opened 1991 is from a search snippet citing Travel Weekly and the Palm Beach Post (via search snippet); Travel Weekly's own page says 'early 1990s'.
  • Whether the 2022 interior renovation covered the guest rooms is not stated; room photos may predate it.
  • No schedule for the balcony renovation: which tower or phase is active Feb 18-22, 2027, and whether rooms near the work are sold, is unknown.
  • Pool lengths, shapes and hours are not published.
  • Beach chair supply, attendant set-up and towel-saving rules are not published; no February review on chair availability was found.
  • Tripadvisor rating and count come from Google Travel's 'reviews on other sites' panel; Tripadvisor itself returned 403 and the Wayback Machine was offline.
  • Google and Tripadvisor review dates are relative ('4 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • No February 2026 review was read; same-season evidence is Jan and Mar 2025 Booking.com reviews.
  • Drive time is free-flow routing (OSRM, Valhalla) without live traffic or drawbridge waits.
  • The resort's FAQ lists the Forbes Five-Star award only through 2024.

Owner-run 1915 B&B in Lake Worth Beach's Old Lucerne district with a garden pool and hot breakfast, a 20-minute walk over the bridge to the beach.

Best for: A couple who wants a quiet, owner-run B&B with breakfast and downtown Lake Worth Beach dinners on foot, and can live with a 20-minute beach walk and a 30-minute ride to Grandma.

Pros
  • King Mango Suite with whirlpool tub, living room and kitchenette

Cons

Insider tips

  • Book the Mango Suite or the Cottage Suite: they are the only king rooms. The rooms page lists the Pineapple Suite as king, but the booking engine and a 2025 guest say queen.
  • Book on the inn's own site: free cancellation runs to 7 days before arrival, versus Feb 4 on Booking.com.
  • If a date shows 'CALL' on the booking calendar, phone 561-533-6900; the inn says it can usually still fit you in.
  • Check-in is 1-9 pm; the minimum check-in age is 21 and children must be over 14.
  • Fri Feb 19 is Lake Worth Beach's bonfire night at the Casino from 6 pm, a short walk over the bridge.
  • Pack insect repellent for the garden and pool.

We couldn’t verify

  • Pool size, heating and hours are not published; a Visit Florida listing reportedly calls it heated (via search snippet). The Booking.com pool and garden photos are older uploads and undated.
  • Booking.com's review list did not load in the headless browser, and Google's 'Lowest score' sort did not apply, so samples are Google Travel's default order.
  • Year the house became a B&B and room renovation dates are not published; 1915 is the house's build year.
  • Whether there is an elevator is not stated (historic house; some rooms are upstairs).
  • Housekeeping frequency not published.
  • Beach chairs: no source mentions any; not confirmed with the inn.
  • The Gulfstream Hotel contractor firing (Sep 2026) and the delayed opening are known only via search snippet; whether work will still be active in Feb 2027 is unconfirmed.
  • Google and Tripadvisor review dates are relative ('4 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • Tripadvisor's 4.6 (197) is as shown on Google Travel; Tripadvisor itself was not read.
  • Drive time is a Google Maps typical range (20-40 min) for a future February afternoon, plus free-flow routers; the 30-minute figure is its midpoint.
  • Expedia and Hotels.com ratings not checked.

Cons
  • No king bed: one queen plus a living-room sofa bed, so it fits the two-beds rule only via the sofa bed
  • Beach is a 15-20 min walk over the George Bush Blvd drawbridge and across A1A, with no beach chairs or umbrella supplied
  • No pool
  • Only a bakery cafe within a 10-min walk; dinner on Atlantic Ave is about 30 min on foot
  • Shared compound: laundry shared with the next-door unit, an owner-only area on the lot and an exterior camera near the back yard
  • Short track record: 19 reviews, all since late 2025; one April 2026 guest flagged cleaning lapses and a loose dishwasher
  • No carbon monoxide alarm reported, no hair dryer listed, and checkout is at 10 am
  • The manager's own site (AOV Rentals) is enquiry-only, so Airbnb is the instant-book channel

Nearby

  • Delray public beach, north end (George Bush Blvd & A1A) · 20 min (Routed 14-15 min; Airbnb and Vrbo say 15; a guest says 15-20)
  • The French Bakery (814 NE 6th Ave) · 10 min (Cafe and bakery; Vrbo lists it as 9 min)
  • Sande's Restaurant · 12 min (Per Vrbo's nearby list; not independently checked)
  • Publix (North Delray Commons, 555 NE 5th Ave) · 15 min (1.15 km by OSRM foot)
  • Pineapple Grove restaurants (NE 2nd Ave) · 23 min (Christina's, Papa's Tapas and others)
  • Atlantic Ave at NE 2nd Ave · 31 min (Downtown Delray's main strip; about a 4-min drive)

Insider tips

  • Walking route to the beach: Palm Trail south to George Bush Blvd, then east over the drawbridge to A1A; the bridge can open for boats, so allow a few extra minutes.
  • At the door keypad, press the checkmark after the code to open; the top button locks (April 2026 guest).
  • Body wash is stored in the closet (host's reply to a March 2026 review); shampoo and a hair dryer are not on the amenities list, so pack your own.
  • The adjacent 2-bedroom unit (AOV Rentals 'Tropical 2bed 1bath Near Beach') can be rented too, for the whole compound and no shared laundry.
  • Bring or rent beach chairs: Oceanside Beach Service rents first-come at Delray's municipal beach; Publix (North Delray Commons) is a 15-min walk for supplies.
  • Your dates overlap the Delray Beach Open (final Sun Feb 21), so book Atlantic Ave dinners ahead.

We couldn’t verify

  • Year built and any renovation of the cottage are not published.
  • Exact minimum stay is not shown; the 4-night Feb 18-22 dates were bookable on Airbnb, so it is at most 4 nights.
  • The North End Beach Access listing and The French Bakery's address are known only via search snippets.
  • Sande's Restaurant's location comes only from Vrbo's nearby list.
  • The registration numbers' issuing bodies are not stated, so a Florida DBPR vacation-rental licence is not confirmed.
  • Construction near the cottage during the dates was not checked against permits or news.
  • Whether the railway is audible was not checked; no reviewer mentions it.
  • The single Vrbo review's text and date were not readable; no Google or Tripadvisor ratings exist for this private guesthouse.
  • Drive times are free-flow router estimates; Google Maps typical daytime traffic was not measured.

Forbes Five-Star, 207-room resort on its own wide beach at the south end of Palm Beach, with two heated oceanfront pools (one adults-only).

Best for: A beach-first luxury stay with the best beach and service on this stretch, if a roughly 30-minute Uber to Grandma's place each visit is acceptable.

How it scores

73Fit score 73/100

Beach access9/10
On its own wide stretch of sand with direct access from the pool deck and attendant beach service; held back from 10 only by open-Atlantic surf, winter man o' war and occasional seaweed.
Drive to Grandma4/10
Google Maps puts a typical Thursday-morning February drive at 30 min (range 22-40) over 14.1 mi, exactly the trip's 30-minute limit and longer than any zone further south.

Cleanliness scores are high on every site (9.1 Booking.com, 4.7/5 Tripadvisor) and even critical reviewers call the rooms very clean; housekeeping is twice daily.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Loungers and umbrellas on the sand are free for guests and set up by beach attendants; one late-fall guest found plenty, but no February report confirms peak-season supply.
Pool8/10
Two heated oceanfront pools, one adults-only, with attentive pool service; kids from the family pool spill into the shared deck, and the adult pool was closed for a team booking in June 2026.
Condition & newness6/10
Fully redesigned in 2018-19 and kept up, but several 2024-26 reviewers call rooms tired or dated (worn carpet, drapes, old bathrooms), including the Palm-View room type booked.
Service9/10
Reviews across sites name front-desk, pool, beach and spa staff for warm, personal service; the complaints are scattered (slow concierge replies, slow room service, a mixed-up bed request).
Quiet7/10
Guests describe peaceful nights on a quiet residential stretch with no party scene, but children at the pools and thin walls in some rooms come up repeatedly.
Walkable dining5/10
Two good restaurants and a café on site, plus the Lake Worth Beach casino restaurants 8-12 minutes south; anything else (downtown Lake Worth, groceries) is a 25+ minute walk or the free house car.
Host reliability8/10
A Four Seasons-managed resort with a 24-hour desk and no reported booking cancellations; docked for June 2026 guests who found the adult pool and beach area closed without warning.

Praised for
  • Personal, warm service; staff learn names and are named in many reviews

Recent trend
Steady: Google 4.7 and Tripadvisor 4.5 with Travelers' Choice 2026, Forbes Five-Star 2026 and Travel + Leisure's No. 1 Florida resort in 2026; the lower scores in 2025-26 focus on value and room wear, not cleanliness or service. Same-season (Jan-Feb) evidence is thin: one January 2026 Tripadvisor stay.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • On its own wide beach: step from the pool deck onto the sand, with free attendant-set loungers and umbrellas
  • Forbes Five-Star service, with staff named in review after review
  • Two heated oceanfront pools, one adults-only
  • Top cleanliness scores (9.1 Booking.com, 4.7/5 Tripadvisor) and twice-daily housekeeping
  • Free house car to downtown Lake Worth, Lantana and Worth Avenue (within 6 miles), plus free beach cruisers
Cons
  • About 30 min to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach in typical daytime traffic (22-40): right at the trip's limit and the longest drive of the zones
  • Some 2024-26 reviewers find rooms tired for a Four Seasons; the Palm-View type is singled out
  • Family resort: children around both pools, and the adult pool shares a deck with the family pool
  • Few restaurants within walking distance and no grocery; the pool-and-beach restaurant closes early evening
  • Mandatory nightly resort fee and paid valet parking

  • Downtown Lake Worth Beach (Lake Ave/Lucerne Ave) · 25 min (Over the Lake Ave bridge; inside the free house-car radius)
  • Publix (Dixie Hwy, Lake Worth Beach) · 33 min (Nearest supermarket; drive or house car)
  • Florie's and Seaway (on site) · 1 min (Plus Florie's Bar, cafe and 24-hour in-room dining)

Insider tips

  • The verified Palm-View room comes as one king or two doubles; a November 2025 guest says ocean views are worth the upgrade, and ground-floor cabana-terrace rooms look onto the pool, not the sea.
  • The free house car only goes within 6 miles, so it won't reach Grandma's place; book an Uber and have it head south to the Lake Ave bridge rather than north to Southern Blvd.
  • A November 2025 guest found the pool-and-beach restaurant closes about 6:30 pm and the main restaurant around 10 pm; Mulligans Beach House and Benny's On The Beach at the Lake Worth Beach casino are 8-12 minutes' walk south.
  • Lake Worth Beach holds its bonfire night at the casino complex on Fri Feb 19 from 6 pm, a short walk south.
  • Complimentary gelato at 3 pm by the pool and free beach-cruiser bikes; daybeds and cabanas cost extra.
  • A June 2026 guest found Palm Beach security road closures slowed drives north on the island; the route to Boynton goes south and west instead.

We couldn’t verify

  • Same-season evidence is thin: one January 2026 Tripadvisor stay and no February review on beach-chair or pool crowding.
  • Pool dimensions, shape and daily hours are not published; 'heated' comes from Booking.com's facility list only.
  • Opening year 1994 is the Four Seasons press-kit opening date; search snippets suggest the building may be older (unverified).
  • Google Maps routed a 22-mile, roughly 40-minute drive north via Southern Blvd when started from the in-resort pin; the 30-minute figure starts from the resort entrance on A1A via the Lake Ave bridge, which matches the router and the hotel next door.
  • The Tripadvisor count (2,692) is from Google's other-sites panel in Oct 2026; Tripadvisor sub-scores and review text come from Wayback snapshots (Mar and Jun 2026) because Tripadvisor blocks direct fetches.
  • Google review dates are relative ('3 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • Booking.com has only 76 reviews, many without comments.
  • The official site blocks image hotlinking; photos are from Booking.com and show the post-2019 design.
  • Whether Fort Partners plans work at the Tideline hotel next door during February 2027 is unknown.
  • Whether lifeguards cover the resort's beach was not confirmed.

28-room gated Key West-style garden hotel with two heated saltwater pools, a block from Delray's public beach and steps from Atlantic Ave.

Best for: A couple who want a quiet, leafy boutique base with a king suite and kitchen, walking to the beach in the morning and Atlantic Ave dinners at night.

How it scores

70Fit score 70/100

Beach access6/10
A 3-5 minute walk, crossing A1A, to Delray's Blue Flag municipal beach, a long, wide public stretch. It is not beachfront, so it sits between the 7 (1-3 min to prime sand) and 4 (4-7 min) anchors.
Drive to Grandma6/10
Routed at 23-25 minutes by car, a little past the 22-minute anchor for a 7. The Atlantic Ave drawbridge (openings at quarter past and quarter to) can add a few minutes.
Cleanliness9/10
Booking.com cleanliness 9.5 and Tripadvisor 4.6, and 2025-26 reviews repeatedly call the rooms super or very clean. One older nitpick is sand tracked into suites.
Beach chairs & umbrellas6/10
Every stay includes two portable beach chairs, so there's no rental competition, but you carry them yourself and no umbrella is mentioned. Umbrellas rent on the beach.
Pool7/10
Two heated saltwater pools for only 28 rooms, one a freeform pool with a rock waterfall. Reviews call them clean and uncrowded, but both are modest courtyard pools.
Condition & newness7/10
A 1952 building, but every room got new furnishings and upgrades in a refresh finished in January 2025, and recent guests call it updated and well maintained.
Service8/10
Booking.com staff score 9.6, and recent reviews name staff (Elliot, Ryan) for going above and beyond. The front desk closes at 9 pm, and older reviews (2021-23) mention unfriendly office staff.
Quiet7/10
Reviews consistently call the gated garden quiet and peaceful, with 10 pm quiet hours. The hotel does post a notice about construction on a neighbouring property from 7 am, and it's unclear whether that will still be going in February.
Walkable dining8/10
About a dozen beach-side and east Atlantic Ave restaurants within a 10-minute walk (Pizza Rustica 3 min, Boston's 5), with downtown's main strip 10-15 min away. There is no grocery within 10 minutes.
Host reliability7/10
A long-running independent hotel whose rooms match its descriptions. But it enforces its deposit rules to the day, and a 2026 Google review and a 2023 Tripadvisor review both describe refunds being refused.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • A 3-5 minute walk to Delray's Blue Flag public beach
  • One Bedroom Suite has a king bedroom, a separate living room and a full kitchen
  • Two beach chairs and beach towels included
  • Two heated saltwater pools in a quiet gated tropical garden
  • Strong recent reviews: Booking.com 9.3, Google 4.7
  • Free on-site parking; restaurants 3-10 minutes on foot
Cons
  • Not beachfront: you cross A1A and carry your own chairs, and there's no umbrella
  • The hotel posts a notice about construction on a neighbouring property from 7 am
  • Strict 50% deposit; cancel inside the window and you lose it
  • No restaurant or breakfast; front desk closes at 9 pm
  • About 25 minutes' drive to Grandma's, plus possible drawbridge waits
  • No grocery within an easy walk

Insider tips

  • Book the One Bedroom Suite (king). The Studio has a single queen and doesn't work for this trip.
  • Booking.com shows no rooms for these dates: book direct or call the hotel, and get the cancellation deadline in writing.
  • The front desk closes at 9 pm, so arrange a late arrival in advance. Check-in is 4 pm; check-out is a guaranteed 12 pm.
  • Sign up early for the free golf-cart ride service to the downtown Atlantic Ave strip (tip the driver), per a 2025 guest.
  • At the beach, a regular guest says turning right (south) is less crowded.
  • Ask to be away from the side facing the neighbouring construction if it is still going on in February.

We couldn’t verify

  • Whether the neighbouring construction named on the policies page will still be going on Feb 18-22, 2027 is unknown (the 100 Gleason St townhomes next door show a 2026 build year; it's unconfirmed that they are the site).
  • The Tripadvisor count (652) is from Google Travel's mirror in Oct 2026; the June 2026 Wayback snapshot showed 647.
  • Elevator: none listed on the official site or Booking.com (two-storey buildings); not confirmed.
  • Pool sizes and opening hours aren't published.
  • Housekeeping frequency isn't published; daily service comes from one guest review and the pet policy.
  • Restaurant count is from OpenStreetMap, which misses some places (e.g. Caffe Luna Rosa), so treat 12 as approximate.
  • No Expedia rating collected (Expedia blocks fetches).

115-room Opal resort on its own private beach in quiet Highland Beach, south of Delray, with attendant-set beach chairs and a heated pool.

Best for: Walking straight onto a quiet private beach every morning with chairs already set up, if you are happy to drive or Uber for dinner and the longest of the trip's drives to Grandma.

How it scores

68Fit score 68/100

Beach access9/10
Directly on its own guests-only beach, steps past the pool deck, on a quiet residential stretch far from the crowded public beaches; lifeguards are not mentioned, and summer seaweed was the only recent beach complaint.
Drive to Grandma4/10
Google Maps puts a typical Thursday-morning February drive at 30 min (range 22-45) over 14.9 mi via I-95 and Boynton Beach Blvd: right at the trip's outer limit.
Cleanliness8/10
Tripadvisor cleanliness 4.5 and 2026 Google reviewers repeatedly say exceptionally clean, impeccable or immaculate; the only recent problem was one Aug 2026 1-star stay that involved a pest issue.
Beach chairs & umbrellas9/10
Two beach chairs, towels and an umbrella per room are included every day and set up by beach attendants on a guests-only beach, with food and drink service; the cost is folded into the mandatory resort fee.
Pool7/10
A heated, palm-lined freeform pool with a whirlpool and a separate children's pool, steps from the beach, with an attendant who clears hogged loungers; it is a mid-size resort pool, and size and hours are not published.
Condition & newness6/10
A late-1960s building fully redone in 2014; most 2026 reviewers find rooms modern and updated, but slow elevators recur and a Mar 2026 guest found a small, dated standard room.
Service8/10
Tripadvisor service 4.4, staff named in many 2026 reviews and a GM who answers nearly every review; complaints are an overloaded valet at busy times and one Aug 2026 report of disrespectful staff.
Quiet8/10
A small resort on a residential, condo-lined stretch of A1A with no nightlife nearby; Tripadvisor sleep quality 4.5 and 2026 guests tag it quiet. The pool bar closes in the evening; weddings and families are the likely noise.
Walkable dining2/10
Latitudes serves three meals on site and the pool bar does lunch, but there is nothing else on the Highland Beach strip: the nearest restaurants and groceries are 33-38 minutes away over the Linton Blvd bridge.
Host reliability7/10
An established Opal Collection resort selling direct with a refundable rate for the dates, but a guest booked for New Year's Eve 2024 was told an hour before check-in that the room was oversold.

Where

Location
Geocoded 2809 S Ocean Blvd with Nominatim, which matches the hotel's own OSM building (still named Holiday Inn Highland Beach). The hotel sits east of A1A on its own private, guests-only beach, so per the run rules the walk ends on its own sand: 0 min to the anchor, about 2 min from a typical room across the pool deck. walk_time.py (OSRM foot) gave 27 min / 2.1 km because it routes to the anchor line's south end at Atlantic Dunes Park; that is the nearest named public beach entrance, north along A1A. Highland Beach itself has no public beach access. Zone delray-south-beach kept: the hotel is about 50 m south of that zone box, at the Highland Beach north tip the zone describes.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • On its own guests-only beach: walk out past the pool to the sand each morning
  • Two beach chairs, towels and an umbrella per room set up daily by attendants
  • Quiet, residential stretch of Highland Beach, far from the busy public beaches
  • Strong recent reviews for cleanliness and staff (Google 4.4 from about 1,500 reviews)
  • Heated pool, whirlpool and Latitudes oceanfront restaurant on site
  • Both king and two-queen rooms, so the bed requirement is easy to meet
Cons
  • About 30 minutes to Grandma's place in typical traffic (22-45), at the trip's limit
  • No restaurants or groceries within walking distance: off-site meals need a car, bike or rideshare
  • Standard-view rooms are about 230 sq ft with no balcony listed
  • Slow elevators keep coming up in reviews
  • Mandatory valet parking and a daily resort fee are extra
  • The hotel does not mention lifeguards on its beach
  • A Dec 2024 guest's prepaid room was oversold on New Year's Eve

Nearby

  • Delray Sands private beach · 2 min (Guests only; past the pool deck; chairs and umbrella set up daily)
  • Latitudes · 1 min (On site: breakfast, lunch and dinner with ocean views)
  • Wave Pool Bar · 1 min (On site: food 11 am-4 pm)
  • Atlantic Dunes Park · 27 min (Nearest named public beach entrance, 2.1 km north on A1A)
  • Trader Joe's · 33 min (1851 S Federal Hwy, 2.65 km routed over the Linton Blvd bridge)
  • The Fresh Market · 34 min (E Linton Blvd, 2.73 km routed)
  • Harvest Seasonal Grill / Another Broken Egg Cafe · 37 min (Federal Hwy and Linton Blvd, 2.9-3.1 km routed)
  • Downtown Delray (Atlantic Ave) (About 2.5 miles north; drive, bike or rideshare)

Insider tips

  • Book direct on reservations.opalcollection.com/delray-sands; the Opal offers page lists a third-night-half-off deal.
  • Standard-view rooms list no balcony; a pool- or ocean-view room adds a furnished balcony.
  • Beachfront ground-floor rooms have patios with loungers facing the sand, but the patios do not open onto the beach.
  • Beach yoga runs Saturdays and Sundays at 9 am, so Feb 20 and 21 fall in your stay.
  • Free cruiser bikes (six, two-hour limit, dawn to dusk) can reach the Linton Blvd shops and restaurants.
  • Guests must be 21+ to check in; check-in is 4 pm, check-out 11 am.
  • Allow extra time to Grandma's: Google's typical range runs up to 45 minutes.

We couldn’t verify

  • Year opened is not published; the GM says only 'late 60s', so year_opened is null.
  • No dated room renovation after December 2014 was found; the site calls rooms 'newly renovated' without a year.
  • Main pool length and pool hours are not published.
  • Front desk hours and housekeeping frequency are not published.
  • Expedia's 9.2/10 is known only via search snippet with no exact count, so it is not listed in ratings.
  • Same-season evidence is thin: only two visible Google reviews date to about Mar 2026; Tripadvisor review text comes from a Feb 2026 Wayback snapshot sorted by 'detailed', so most of it is from 2023-2025.
  • Google review dates are relative ('4 months ago') and converted to approximate months; the Aug 2026 1-star review's full text was truncated, so its details come from the GM's reply.
  • Restaurant and grocery counts come from Nominatim searches plus OSRM foot routes; Overpass was unavailable.
  • Beach width for Feb 2027 not checked: whether Delray's 2026 south-beach renourishment (to south of Atlantic Dunes Park) reached this beach is unconfirmed.
  • Whether the hotel's beach has lifeguards is not stated; sargassum seasonality is via search snippet (run context).

157-room Autograph Collection hotel on East Atlantic Ave, renovated 2025, a 5-minute walk to Delray's public beach plus a private beach club.

Best for: A couple who wants a polished, walkable Atlantic Ave base with a private beach club, and can live with a roughly 28-minute ride to Grandma's.

How it scores

68Fit score 68/100

Beach access5/10
Not on the sand: a 5-minute walk east on Atlantic Ave and across A1A to Delray's wide, lifeguarded public beach, well inside the 20-minute limit. The private Beach Club with loungers is 15 minutes' walk south or a hotel shuttle ride.
Drive to Grandma5/10
Google Maps puts a typical Thursday-morning February drive at 28 min (range 20-40) over 11.0 mi, inside the 30-minute limit but well past the 22-minute anchor.
Cleanliness8/10
Booking.com and Priceline both score cleanliness 9.4 and guests call rooms spotless or immaculate, with one sewage-odour room move in January 2026.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Loungers, umbrellas and towels at the private Beach Club come with hotel guests' club access, with food and drink service on the sand; the catch is a shuttle or 15-minute walk, and members share the club.
Pool7/10
Two heated pools: a rectangular resort pool with cabanas and a bar at the hotel, plus the oceanfront Beach Club pool; one winter guest found the hotel pool mostly in shade.
Condition & newness9/10
Opened 2009 and fully redesigned in a renovation finished November 2025, so rooms are about 15 months old at the trip; a few early maintenance slips were reported.
Service7/10
Staff are named in review after review (Booking.com staff 9.3), but the switch to Marriott's systems brought recurring billing errors, an unanswered front-desk phone and slow check-ins in winter 2025-26.
Quiet6/10
Mostly calm for a Main Street hotel, but several reviewers mention street noise from busy Atlantic Ave, a noisy service elevator and a loud lobby, and the Delray Beach Open fills downtown on Feb 18-21.
Walkable dining9/10
Restaurants start at the door: about 13 mapped sit-down places within a 10-minute walk on East Atlantic Ave and A1A, plus four on-site venues; the nearest full supermarket is a 20-minute walk.
Host reliability6/10
A branded hotel with a 24-hour desk that honours bookings, but billing was the weak spot after the Marriott switch: duplicate charges, payments not showing, wrong rooms assigned.

Recent trend
Reopened Nov 2025 after the renovation. Winter 2025-26 reviews were mixed, with service and billing teething problems; from spring 2026 Booking.com reviews are almost all 10/10. Same-season (Jan-Mar 2026) evidence exists and is the most critical.

Recent reviews, paraphrased (not exact quotes):

  • “February stay as a couple: spacious, immaculately clean room with a big, well-lit bathroom; a lovely pool and hot tub and a quick shuttle to the beach club; walkable to shops, cafes and the beach; friendly staff and a recommended spa.”Tripadvisor, 2026-02
  • “February couple: great location and nice rooms, but could not check in until 6 pm with no warning, turndown was hit-and-miss, and a minibar billing error took three days and a dismissive manager to fix.”Tripadvisor, 2026-02
  • “Twelve-night January stay: large, lovely balcony room, but the front desk never answered the phone, the area was very noisy, the pool sat mostly in shade, and the beach, tennis and golf all needed the shuttle.”4/10, Booking.com, 2026-01-05
  • “March spring-break family: lovely hotel and warm staff, but a beach-renourishment pipe ran across the beach club in front of the chairs, hiding the ocean, and nobody followed up on their complaint.”Tripadvisor, 2026-03

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • 5-minute walk to Delray's public beach at the end of Atlantic Ave
  • Private Beach Club with loungers, umbrellas, pool and food service, plus a hotel shuttle
  • Rooms fully redesigned in 2025 (Autograph Collection since Nov 2025)
  • Strong scores: Booking.com 9.0 with cleanliness 9.4, Tripadvisor 4.8
  • Restaurants at the door on East Atlantic Ave, four on-site venues and a spa
Cons
  • About 28 minutes by car to Grandma's in typical traffic, near the 30-minute limit
  • Recurring billing errors and an unreachable front desk in winter 2025-26 reviews
  • Atlantic Ave street noise; some rooms sit by the service elevator
  • The verified Interior King is an inward-facing room; one April 2026 guest got a wall view
  • Hotel pool is largely shaded; the sunny oceanfront pool is at the Beach Club

Nearby

  • Delray Beach public beach (Atlantic Ave entrance, by the beach pavilion) · 5 min (East on Atlantic Ave, across A1A at the signal)
  • The Seagate Beach Club (401 S Ocean Blvd) · 15 min (Private club for hotel guests and members; hotel shuttle)
  • Pizza Rustica and Del Fuego (East Atlantic Ave) · 2 min
  • Boston's on the Beach (A1A) · 4 min
  • Deck 84 · 5 min (Across the Atlantic Ave drawbridge)
  • Publix (555 NE 5th Ave) · 21 min (Nearest full supermarket; The Gate cafe on site sells grab-and-go)

Insider tips

  • For a morning beach walk, head 5 minutes east on Atlantic Ave to the public beach; the private Beach Club (loungers, pool, Mr. Seas) is 1.2 km south on A1A, so use the hotel's chauffeured car.
  • Ask the concierge in person to book the shuttle: a January 2026 guest could not get through on the phones.
  • Mr. Seas at the Beach Club runs happy hour 4-6 pm daily with 50% off bar drinks (bar only).
  • Check your folio at checkout: several 2025-26 reviewers had to chase billing errors.
  • The Delray Beach Open runs through Feb 21, so downtown restaurants and parking are busier Feb 19-21; book dinner ahead.
  • Pool-view and balcony rooms look outward; Interior Kings face inward.

We couldn’t verify

  • Hotel pool dimensions are not published.
  • Beach Club chair supply, attendant set-up and any reservation policy for hotel guests are not published; inferred from Booking.com's amenity list, the resort-fee terms, official photos and reviews.
  • Expedia and Hotels.com ratings not checked (sites block automated access).
  • Tripadvisor rating and count come from a May 2026 Wayback capture; Google's panel showed 918 Tripadvisor reviews in Oct 2026. Tripadvisor star ratings were not visible in the archived review text, so those samples have no rating.
  • Year opened (2009) comes from the hotel's Nov 2025 press release only.
  • Construction near the hotel in Feb 2027 is unconfirmed: an FDOT A1A resurfacing project (Atlantic Ave to Linton Blvd) was due to finish in spring 2026 (via search snippet).
  • Grocery count is from OpenStreetMap, which may miss small markets.

Renovated 1930s-40s 2-bed cottage a few houses off Atlantic Ave: California King, small private heated pool, 11-min walk to Delray's beach.

Best for: A couple who want a whole cottage with a king bed and a private heated dip pool, steps from Atlantic Ave dinners and an easy walk or bike ride to Delray's main beach.

How it scores

66Fit score 66/100

Beach access4/10
Not on the sand: Delray's guarded municipal beach at E Atlantic Ave is about an 11-min walk over the Atlantic Ave drawbridge and across A1A, well inside the trip's 20-min limit but past the rubric's 8-min mark; supplied bikes cut it to a few minutes.
Drive to Grandma5/10
Google Maps gives 28 min and 10.8 mi to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach on a weekday late morning (typically 20-40 min), between the rubric's 22- and 30-min anchors; free-flow routers say 22-24 min, so heavy traffic can push it past 30.
Cleanliness8/10
Cleanliness 4.9 on Airbnb and 2024-2026 guests call it clean and well stocked; the one lapse was a Jan 2024 3-star stay with leftover food, dirty dishes and a stained comforter, which the host replaced within hours.
Beach chairs & umbrellas6/10
The house supplies its own beach chairs, umbrella and bikes, so there is no rental fee or scramble, but you carry them about 11 min each way (or bike) and there is no attendant setup.
Pool3/10
A private, heated pool you never share, but it is a small round above-ground pool, good for cooling off rather than swimming, with no gate or lock.
Condition & newness8/10
A 1930s-40s cottage renovated around 2020 with a new kitchen, A/C, pool and patio; recent guests call it comfortable and well kept, but rooms are small and there is one bathroom.
Service9/10
Host AJ is named in most reviews for quick, helpful replies (Communication 5.0, Check-in 5.0), gives local tips and fixed the one reported problem within hours; no front desk.
Quiet7/10
Guests repeatedly call Palm Square a quiet side street with a peaceful backyard, but Atlantic Ave's bars are a block away and one guest heard early-morning delivery trucks.
Walkable dining10/10
The east end of Atlantic Ave's restaurant strip is a 2-3 min walk (The Bridge Cafe, Deck 84, Hawkers, Le Colonial), with about 29 restaurants within 600 m; there is no grocery within 10 min.
Host reliability8/10
Nearly seven years hosting this one home with 66 reviews at 4.95, a Guest favorite badge, Accuracy 4.9 and no reported cancellations; not a Superhost, response rate not shown, and only three reviews in the last 12 months.

Insider tips

  • The 4-night Feb 18-22 dates were bookable on Airbnb, so the minimum stay is 4 nights or fewer.
  • Cancellation offered for these dates: free for 24 hours after booking.
  • Take the supplied bikes to the beach: the 11-min walk becomes a few minutes, and chairs and umbrella come from the house.
  • Host and guests recommend the free Freebee ride app (golf carts and shuttles) for getting around downtown Delray.
  • Two cars fit on the shared driveway; any extra car uses the adjacent public lot.
  • Your dates overlap the Delray Beach Open tennis (through Feb 21) downtown, so book Atlantic Ave dinners ahead.
  • Man o' war season runs Nov-Apr: watch for the purple flag at the lifeguard stands.

We couldn’t verify

Updated 2-bed townhouse with a king en-suite and a private heated spa-style pool, a 12-14 min walk over the George Bush Blvd bridge to Delray's beach.

Best for: Two adults who want a king en-suite, a private warm pool and supplied beach gear, a 12-14 min walk to Delray's north beach and about 22 min from Grandma's, and who don't mind a small spa-style pool and walking or taking the Freebee to dinner.

Insider tips

  • Brampton Park's own site quotes the same cottage, but booking direct is by enquiry, phone or text (561-221-1466) or a 48-hour hold; Airbnb is the instant option.
  • Brampton Park's terms require ID verification after booking and a minimum renter age of 25.
  • Take the supplied chairs and umbrella; time the walk to cross the Atlantic Ave drawbridge between its quarter-past and quarter-to openings.
  • The Delray Beach Open runs Feb 12-21, 2027 at the tennis center about an 18-minute walk west, so book Atlantic Ave dinners ahead on Feb 19-21.
  • Parking for 2 cars on the private driveway saves paying for downtown or beach meters.

All-suite ex-Residence Inn on East Atlantic Ave, a 5-6 minute walk to Delray's public beach, with kitchenettes, a heated pool and hot tub.

Best for: A couple who wants to walk to Delray's main public beach in the morning and to Atlantic Ave restaurants at night, with a kitchenette suite and a drive to Grandma's of under half an hour.

How it scores

60Fit score 60/100

Beach access5/10
A 5-6 minute walk east along Atlantic Ave and over A1A at a signalised crossing to Delray's lifeguarded public beach: inside the rubric's 4-7 minute band, but it is a short walk to good public sand, not beachfront.
Drive to Grandma6/10
About 23-24 minutes and 11-12 miles by car with no traffic, a little past the 22-minute anchor and inside the 30-minute limit; the route crosses the Atlantic Ave drawbridge.
Cleanliness7/10
2026 Google reviewers keep calling the rooms very clean, but Tripadvisor's cleanliness sub-score is only 4.0 and older stays reported missed housekeeping and a dirty breakfast area.
Beach chairs & umbrellas1/10
The hotel supplies no beach chairs or umbrellas: its FAQ says to bring your own or rent from the vendor on the beach.
Pool6/10
One heated, mid-size oval pool plus a hot tub on a sunny deck: a good swim pool, but it backs onto Atlantic Ave and a March 2023 guest saw loungers towel-saved before sunrise.
Condition & newness7/10
Guest suites were fully renovated in 2023 and 2026 reviews call them stunning and spacious, but the building itself is an older ex-Residence Inn with small bathrooms.
Service7/10
2026 reviews name front-desk staff (Lovelie), praise early check-ins, an upgrade and mid-stay text check-ins, and the owner answers every review; Tripadvisor's 4.0 service score reflects older complaints about understaffing and unhelpful desk staff.
Quiet6/10
Many 2026 guests tag it quiet, but it sits right on busy East Atlantic Ave: street noise reaches the pool and upper floors, and one stack of rooms backs onto the elevators.
Walkable dining8/10
A cluster of beach-end restaurants is 2-5 minutes away (Tripadvisor counts 31 within 0.3 mi) and downtown's main Atlantic Ave strip starts over the bridge about 8 minutes west, but the nearest grocery is over 20 minutes on foot.
Host reliability7/10
An Opal Collection hotel with a staffed front desk that answers every review and refunded a late-cancelled deposit as an exception, though one 2024 group got smaller suites than the photos suggested.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • About a 5-6 minute walk to Delray's lifeguarded public beach at the end of Atlantic Ave
  • King studio suites with kitchenettes; rooms fully renovated in 2023
  • Heated pool and hot tub
  • Breakfast buffet, self-parking, Wi-Fi and pool towels included in the resort fee
  • Restaurants 2 minutes away; downtown's Atlantic Ave strip about 8 minutes west
  • Strong 2026 Google reviews (4.5 from 825) that name front-desk staff
  • About 23-24 minutes by car to Grandma's place
Cons
  • No beach chairs or umbrellas: bring your own or rent on the sand
  • On busy Atlantic Ave: street noise at the pool and on street-side balconies; '03' rooms back onto the elevators
  • Tripadvisor only 3.8/5 (#8 of 13 in Delray), far below Google
  • Breakfast repeatedly called basic; no on-site restaurant
  • Mandatory daily resort fee
  • No grocery within a 20-minute walk
  • Small bathrooms with little counter space

Insider tips

  • Ask for a room off the '03' stack, which backs onto the elevators, and away from the Atlantic Ave side if you sleep lightly (Jan 2025 Tripadvisor tip).
  • Bring beach chairs or rent from Oceanside Beach Service on the sand; the hotel only supplies pool towels.
  • The lobby breakfast buffet runs 6:30-9:30 am on weekdays and 7-10 am at weekends, so it works before an early beach walk.
  • The drive to Grandma's crosses the Atlantic Ave drawbridge, which opens at quarter past and quarter to the hour.
  • The person booking must be 21 or older; check-in is 4 pm and check-out 11 am.
  • It sells direct: it is not on Booking.com and Google lists only the official site, so book on Opal's own engine.
  • Recent guests got early check-in and a balcony upgrade by asking at the desk.
  • The Delray Beach Open runs to Feb 21 at the tennis center about 20 minutes' walk west, so downtown is busy that weekend.

We couldn’t verify

  • Year opened is unverified: a search summary says the Residence Inn opened in 2001 (via search snippet); the hotel's FAQ gives 11 floors and Tripadvisor 131 rooms.
  • Expedia's score was not readable (bot block); a search summary reports 9.4/10 from 1,000+ reviews (via search snippet), so it is not listed in ratings. The hotel is not on Booking.com.
  • Pool length and official hours are not published; the dusk closing comes from a guest's description of a sign.
  • Housekeeping frequency is not stated on the official site.
  • Construction near the hotel during the dates was not checked beyond a search summary that puts Atlantic Crossing, west of the Intracoastal, still building into 2027 (via search snippet).
  • Google review dates are relative ('2 months ago') and converted to approximate months; recent Google reviews are almost uniformly 5/5, while Tripadvisor's live site was blocked, so its newest readable text is the Feb 2026 Wayback page plus Google's Tripadvisor excerpts.
  • No February 2026 reviews were found; the nearest same-season stays are Jan and Mar 2025.
  • The 2023 renovation date comes from one press item; exterior and pool photos are from 2022, the room photos from 2026.

134-room beachfront hotel next to the Four Seasons and Kreusler Park, renovated in 2023 and sold in Sept 2026; spa closed and dining scaled back.

Best for: A couple who want to step straight onto a quiet beach with chairs included and can accept a hotel in transition, plus a drive to Grandma's at the 30-minute limit.

How it scores

59Fit score 59/100

Beach access8/10
Directly on a quiet, well-reviewed stretch of sand with the public R.G. Kreusler Park entrance next door, so the morning beach walk is a couple of minutes; not a 10 because the pool sits on the street side and this South End beach has no reported calm-water or crowd advantage over its neighbours.
Drive to Grandma5/10
Google Maps puts a Thursday-morning February drive at 28 minutes (typically 22-40) over 13.9 mi, just inside the 30-minute limit but with a real chance of running over it in traffic or at a drawbridge.
Cleanliness6/10
Booking.com cleanliness 8.2 and Tripadvisor 4.0 with many 2026 guests calling rooms very clean, but recent low reviews report hallway odours, cigarette smell in a non-smoking room and dirty corners (fridge, shower, terrace cushions), so it is clean with recurring lapses.
Beach chairs & umbrellas8/10
Two beach chairs and an umbrella per room plus towel service come with the resort fee, set up by beach staff that reviewers name; no same-season report of shortages, though Feb 2026 reviews describe the hotel as short-staffed.
Pool6/10
One heated, palm-ringed rectangular pool with a hot tub and pool bar; decent for relaxing, but it is on the street side rather than the ocean, its size is unpublished and one reviewer called the pool and hot tub dirty.
Condition & newness5/10
Rooms were fully redone in 2023, which should score high, but 2025-26 reviews keep reporting elevator outages, electrical faults, loud AC and a tired exterior, and the new owner's plans are unknown.
Service5/10
Front-desk staff such as Noel are named warmly in many 2026 reviews, but Booking.com staff is only 7.7 and Tripadvisor service 3.4, with repeated reports of short staffing, slow food and drinks, undisclosed fees and a few rude encounters.
Quiet6/10
A small hotel on a residential stretch with a quiet private beach and no party scene, but recent reviews report a barking dog next door (pet-friendly), loud room AC, thin walls and earlier false fire alarms.
Walkable dining5/10
On-site breakfast, daytime dining and a bar, with dinner only promised from Nov 6, 2026; the Four Seasons restaurants are next door and the Lake Worth Beach casino eateries 6-9 minutes away, but downtown Lake Worth and groceries are a 25-30 minute walk.
Host reliability4/10
Bookings are sold on the hotel's own engine and major OTAs, but the hotel closed briefly during the Sept 2026 sale, still advertises spa services the spa page says won't return until Nov 2027, and recent guests report undisclosed fees, missing restaurant service and a slow deposit refund.

1980
Renovated
2023 · Built in 1980 and later run as The Omphoy; Jeff Greene owned it from 2011 and finished a major renovation of rooms (new floors, marble, furniture, rain showers) and public areas in 2023-early 2024. Fort Partners, owner of the Four Seasons next door, bought it on Sept 15, 2026; staff said Sept 18 that the resort was closed until the next month, and Amalfi and Mizu were closed. As of Oct 2026 the site lists breakfast, daytime dining, pool/beach service and a bar, says dinner starts Nov 6, and shows the spa as 'Coming Soon, November 2027', so no spa during the trip. No rebrand or renovation plan has been announced.
Condition
Rooms still read as fresh in many 2026 Google reviews, but recurring 2025-26 reviews mention one of the two elevators out for days, flaky electrics and lighting, loud room AC, a run-down exterior and driveway, and a July 2026 guest called the rooms a little dated.

  • Short staffing, elevator outages and noisy AC in Feb 2026 reviews

Insider tips

  • Before booking, call to confirm the restaurant, breakfast and bar hours for Feb 18-22; dinner is only promised from Nov 6, 2026.
  • The spa won't reopen until Nov 2027 per the official site, despite older listings mentioning it.
  • Book the Two Queen or King Balcony Garden View; the pool sits on the A1A side, so garden rooms overlook palms and the pool, not the ocean.
  • Ask before checking in early: a July 2026 guest was charged for a 1 pm check-in without warning. Self-parking exists even if valet takes the keys.
  • Check-in 4 pm, check-out 11 am; the person checking in must be 21+ with photo ID and a card for the damage deposit.
  • Allow 40 minutes for the drive to Grandma's at busy times (Lake Ave bridge, I-95, Boynton Beach Blvd).
  • Lake Worth Beach's bonfire night is Fri Feb 19 from 6 pm, a 9-minute walk south along A1A.
  • Ask for a room away from pet guests if you're a light sleeper.

We couldn’t verify

  • Post-sale operations are unconfirmed: which restaurant(s), breakfast and bar will run Feb 18-22, 2027, and whether Fort Partners plans renovation work around the trip, are not published.
  • The spa page says 'November 2027'; it could be a typo for 2026, but either way no spa reopening before February is confirmed.
  • Tripadvisor rating and count (3.8, 106) come from Google Travel's 'reviews on other sites' panel; Tripadvisor itself was not reachable, and its Jan 2026 Wayback snapshot showed 3.7 on 80 reviews.
  • Priceline rating and count come from the same Google Travel panel; no Priceline URL.
  • Google review dates are relative ('2 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • Pool size and hours are not published; Booking.com lists the pool as seasonal.
  • Beach chair supply is from Booking.com's fine print; the hotel's own site doesn't state it, and no February report on chair availability was found.
  • Year 1980 is the build year (Commercial Observer); the hotel's opening year under its earlier names is not confirmed.
  • Drive time uses Google Maps' typical-traffic estimate and Valhalla free-flow routing; the OSRM car and foot routers refused connections.
  • Restaurant count within 10 minutes is from OpenStreetMap and Booking.com's nearby list; whether the Four Seasons restaurants take non-guests in February was not checked.

Quirky 1-bedroom king unit in a small garden complex with a koi pond, about a block from Delray's Atlantic Ave beach; beach gear included, no pool.

Best for: A couple who wants to walk to Delray's main beach and the Atlantic Ave restaurants in minutes, likes a quirky tropical-garden setting and doesn't need a pool or polished finishes.

  • The 4-night Feb 18-22 dates were bookable, so the minimum stay is 4 nights or fewer.

Pros and cons for you

Pros
  • Two-queen rooms fit the party; spacious, modern rooms in a 2019 building
  • Atlantic Ave's restaurants and shops are a 3-4 minute walk
  • Heated rooftop pool and bar with ocean views
  • About 22-23 minutes by car to Grandma's place in Boynton Beach
  • Free cancellation available on the verified Booking.com room
Cons
  • Not on the beach: a 17-minute walk over the Atlantic Ave drawbridge, crossing US-1 and A1A
  • No beach chairs or umbrellas from the hotel
  • Paid parking and no free breakfast
  • Some recent housekeeping and shower complaints
  • Delray Beach Open weekend (Feb 19-21) makes downtown busier

Nearby

  • Delray Beach public beach (Atlantic Ave entrance at A1A) · 17 min (Via Atlantic Ave and its drawbridge; chairs and umbrellas rented on the sand.)
  • Atlantic Ave restaurant strip (SE 6th Ave corner) · 4 min (About 40 restaurants and cafes within roughly 600 m.)
  • Amar Mediterranean Kitchen & Bar · 3 min (About 220 m straight-line (OSM).)
  • The Bistro and Reef rooftop bar · 0 min (On site: breakfast, dinner, Starbucks drinks; rooftop bar by the pool.)
  • Publix (555 NE 5th Ave) · 17 min (Nearest full supermarket; a small market is in the hotel lobby.)
  • Delray Beach Tennis Center (About 0.7 mi per Booking.com; Delray Beach Open runs Feb 12-21, 2027.)
  • Freebee rides (Free on-demand rides along the Atlantic Ave strip (via a 2024 guest review).)

Insider tips

  • Ask for a higher floor away from the rooftop pool for quiet; odd-numbered rooms face the water, per a 2024 guest.
  • The walk to the beach crosses the Atlantic Ave drawbridge, which opens at quarter past and quarter to the hour; allow a few extra minutes.
  • Beach chairs and umbrellas are rented at the municipal beach, first come, first served; go early on the Feb 20-21 weekend.
  • The free Freebee ride service covers the Atlantic Ave strip if you don't want to walk back from the beach.
  • Minimum check-in age is 21; check-in 4 pm, check-out 11 am.

We couldn’t verify

  • Marriott.com blocks bots; official facts come from a Feb 2026 Wayback copy and may have changed.
  • Rooftop pool dimensions not published.
  • No renovation since the October 2019 opening was found; last_renovated is null.
  • Tripadvisor count 224 and the Trip.com and Marriott.com ratings come from Google's 'reviews on other travel sites' panel (Oct 2026); the Feb 2026 Tripadvisor snapshot showed 217.
  • Google review dates are relative ('7 months ago') and converted to approximate months.
  • Drive times are free-flow router estimates without live traffic; February daytime traffic may add several minutes.
  • Restaurant count is an OSM/Nominatim search within 600 m straight-line, not a routed 10-minute walk.
  • Construction near the hotel during Feb 2027 not checked against city planning sources.
  • Whether a concierge or beach-towel loan is offered is unknown.

Insider tips

  • Message Casey before booking to confirm the king bed and ask which unit is farthest from the shared courtyard; she lists #1 and #4 at the same address too.
  • Pack a warm layer: February lows average about 60°F and heat comes from a portable heater.
  • Bring laundry detergent for the shared washers and dryers in the rear garage.
  • Fri Feb 19 is Lake Worth Beach bonfire night at the Casino from 6 pm, at the end of your beach walk.
  • Self check-in by smart lock from 3 pm; checkout is 10 am.
